scope: First three Tycho evidence-backed pilots only; manually specified evaluation questions, not executed AI-agent or MCP benchmarks.
status: human-independent question set; expected answer elements are author assertions requiring independent review

items.question: What is the precise boundary for L, lambda and W?
items.expected_elements: Mean in-boundary work equals completed/admitted steady flow times mean residence time; boundary and units required
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not infer thread count

items.question: Can p99 replace W in Little's Law?
items.expected_elements: No; W is a mean, not a percentile; include synthetic example
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not claim a p99 capacity

items.question: What does the Debezium Outbox Event Router use for event ID and Kafka key by default?
items.expected_elements: Unique event ID is header; aggregateid controls key; version-specific
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not equate event ID with business ID

items.question: What does Kubernetes maxSurge configure?
items.expected_elements: Extra replicas relative to desired count in a rolling deployment; may affect temporary capacity
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not assert client success

items.question: What is the distinction between RTO and RPO?
items.expected_elements: RTO is tolerated restoration time, RPO tolerated data recovery point gap
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not claim these are measured

items.question: Why can high user counts coexist with low request arrival rates?
items.expected_elements: Registered users, active sessions and request production are different; need behavior assumptions
items.evidence_basis: Tycho requirements model plus queueing page
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not derive RPS from registered users alone

items.question: Why is the outbox not an exactly-once external business guarantee?
items.expected_elements: Atomic source state/outbox commit stops at local database; relay and consumer need dedup/reconciliation
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not promise global exactly once

items.question: Why can binary rollback fail after a deployment succeeds?
items.expected_elements: N+1 may write incompatible persistent data; old N can no longer read; forward fix/restore needed
items.evidence_basis: Kubernetes Deployment rollback plus Tycho synthetic sequence
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not equate route reversal with DB rollback

items.question: How do request idempotency keys differ from event IDs?
items.expected_elements: Client logical command identity versus immutable event publication identity; scope, parameter matching and retention
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not assume HTTP method alone enforces application key

items.question: When is a closed load model preferable to an open model?
items.expected_elements: When fixed clients await completion/think time; depends on audience behavior
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not rank models universally

items.question: When is polling an outbox preferable to CDC?
items.expected_elements: Based on DB/connector constraints and complexity/latency; weigh scan overhead and replay
items.evidence_basis: Debezium outbox docs; Tycho option table
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not invent measured latencies

items.question: When might blue/green beat rolling deployment?
items.expected_elements: Fast traffic switch and isolated preview; costs duplicate capacity, state compatibility still needed
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not claim data rollback

items.question: Does adding app threads or a larger connection pool solve backlog growth?
items.expected_elements: Not necessarily; requires downstream demand, queue and service measurements
items.evidence_basis: Kim & Whitt 2013 and Tycho synthetic load
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not choose specific pool size

items.question: An HTTP reply is lost after a registration committed. What prevents a second reservation?
items.expected_elements: Same request key/parameters and DB-enforced outcome replay, concurrency-safe dedup needed
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not claim generic POST is idempotent

items.question: A relay crashes after broker acknowledgement is lost. Can the event repeat?
items.expected_elements: Yes, duplicate delivery is possible; consumer needs event-ID dedup in same local transaction as effect
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not claim broker ack fixes consumer effect

items.question: What happens to admitted backlog when offers=200/s and exits=150/s for 30s?
items.expected_elements: Under no rejection/abandonment and admitted=offered, grows by 1500 synthetic operations
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not treat burst as stationary

items.question: A canary is ready but p99 client latency worsens. Is promotion safe?
items.expected_elements: No evidence of user SLO; freeze progression, inspect client metrics, samples and invariants
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not equate readiness with user-level quality

items.question: A new app version removes a database column read by old instances. What changes?
items.expected_elements: Mixed-version contract breaks; expand/contract or forward migration and tests needed
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not assume rollback restores old column

items.question: What happens to outbox correctness when event keys switch from aggregate ID to random IDs?
items.expected_elements: Per-aggregate partition ordering may be lost; key migration needs consumer compatibility/replay plan
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not claim global ordering

items.question: A traffic peak becomes burstier but average RPS stays constant. Does Little's Law determine p99?
items.expected_elements: No; tail depends on variability/queueing; measure distribution and admission
items.evidence_basis: Kim & Whitt finite windows; k6 models
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not infer p99 from mean

items.question: A dashboard shows λW=2 but observed mean N=1 during a five-second window. Is the law false?
items.expected_elements: No: unfinished edge customer counted across mismatched window; cite finite-window caveat
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not call finite sample proof of theorem failure

items.question: A deployment is Available but registration failures occur. Which status wins?
items.expected_elements: Different measured scopes; service-level SLI fails despite controller health
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: Do not collapse health into availability promise

items.question: An API has 100,000 registered users and p99=2s. Choose exact instance and database pool counts.
items.expected_elements: Insufficient evidence; demand mix, mean residence, capacity, failure headroom, test needed
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: No exact sizing numbers

items.question: The system uses Debezium outbox. Prove external payments are applied exactly once.
items.expected_elements: Insufficient evidence; external provider, dedup retention and reconciliation need validation
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: No global exactly-once guarantee

items.question: The deployment controller reports success. Claim RPO=0 under region failure.
items.expected_elements: Insufficient evidence; requires restore point, DR drills, actual data lag and user acceptance
items.forbidden_unsupported_claim: No fake DR measurement
